title: runtime/policies.json — fully-resolved policy tables (ADR-005 Part 2, ADR-003 §8)
description: Compiled, flat, complete. The tighten-only merge algebra runs in the compiler (stage 5); a runtime never merges policy. Matrix completeness over the intent set is proved at compile time, not by this schema.

confirmation.description: intent id → confirmation policy. High-cost actions must resolve to 'always' (medical wrong-action budget).

^[A-Za-z0-9_. -]+$.description: always = the intent declares a followup and confirms on every turn; never = it fires directly. There is deliberately no confidence-conditional value: a band that decides when to ask was removed in favour of a single fire threshold (docs/confirm-gate-diagnosis.md), and an app contract cannot depend on where the classifier happened to land.

agreement.description: Relaxed bar applied when two INDEPENDENT recognisers name the same intent — a keyword rule and the model, or the model and the semantic head. Corroboration offsets the softmax diffusion of a large label space, so a turn both stages agree on need only clear this instead of `confidence`. It is evidence strength, not a confidence: the reported confidence stays the model's calibrated probability.

oov_reject.description: Share of an utterance's tokens that may be absent from the intent model's vocabulary before the turn is refused. A TF-IDF vector has one slot per known term and none for anything else, so an unknown word does not lower the score — it vanishes, and 'turn off toshiba' produces a vector bit-identical to 'turn off'. Confidence is therefore honest about an input the model was never given, and no confidence threshold can recover the difference. Tokenise exactly as the featurizer does (default sklearn token_pattern) and compare against the model's UNIGRAM vocabulary. MUST be applied together with `oov_bypass`. The value is a property of the vocabulary shipped with it: a client using the pruned head must use the ratio fitted for that head.

oov_bypass.description: Confidence at or above which the out-of-vocabulary guard stands down. REQUIRED WHENEVER `oov_reject` IS PRESENT — a client applying the ratio without this ceiling refuses entity values, which are out-of-vocabulary by nature: a contact name, a brand or a free-text topic can never all be in a finite vocabulary, so 'send a message to john' (25% unknown, confidence 1.000) and 'stream from netflix' (33% unknown, 0.996) are real commands while 'help me find a paper' (25% unknown, 0.771) is not. The ratio cannot separate those; the confidence can. An unknown token is evidence of being out of scope only when the REST of the utterance is also ambiguous.
